one_line: Six teams, forty runners, and a queue that is always somebody else's fault.
monitor_rationale: reports queue depth and long holds; four months, then we look again

ladder.label: queue-share
ladder.text: No team holds more than a third of the runners for longer than an hour.

shared.label: capacity-buys
shared.text: New capacity is agreed before it is bought, because everyone pays for it.

access.label: every-team-builds
access.text: Every team can submit to the farm without asking anybody.

inner_a.label: runner-images-pinned
inner_a.text: A runner image is pinned to a digest and rebuilt, never mutated in place.

inner_b.label: runner-clean
inner_b.text: A runner is returned to its image between jobs.

clash_a.label: fair-queue
clash_a.text: Jobs are served in the order they arrive.

clash_b.label: release-first
clash_b.text: A release build jumps the queue, because a release that waits is an outage that waits.

extra.label: job-labels
extra.text: A job carries the team that submitted it as a label.

policy.root: One reasoned objection stops a change. Amending something ranked a principle takes the group. Anything we cannot roll back is not decided by silence.
policy.inner: Whoever maintains the runner images decides the runners.
policy.unheld: Storage is decided by whoever holds it.
policy.ladder: The first time we ask. The second time the group asks together. The third time the answer is no.
policy.inner_amended: Two of us have to object before a runner change stops.

inner_proposal.text: add a warm cache layer to the runner image
inner_proposal.because: a cache baked into the digest is still pinned and still reproducible

inner_objection: a cache in the image means two runs on the same digest can differ, which is the thing the pin was for

unheld_proposal.text: move build artifacts to the cheaper cold bucket after a week

monitor_watch.about: one team held thirty runners for three hours
monitor_watch.because: the hold ran past an hour and past a third of the farm
monitor_watch.dismissal: these two do not really conflict

ladder_subject.about: holding more than a third of the farm
ladder_subject.first: run the full matrix on every push for the migration week
ladder_subject.second: run the full matrix again for the follow-up migration
ladder_subject.third: run the full matrix nightly from now on
ladder_subject.because: a third of the farm held for hours is every other team's build waiting behind it
ladder_subject.ruling_1: we let the migration week stand
ladder_subject.ruling_2: the group agreed one more, then no more

other_subject.text: submit the soak tests with no timeout set

clash.text: let the release pipeline preempt running jobs, not just queued ones
clash.because_a: a queue that can be jumped is not a queue, and every team will find a reason to be a release
clash.because_b: a release that waits behind a soak test is an outage that waits behind a soak test
clash.carried: preemption is bounded to the release branch and the branch is protected, so the escape hatch has a lock on it; revisit when a second branch needs it

amend_convention.text: drop the team label and read the team off the branch prefix
amend_convention.because: the prefix is already there and the label is forgotten half the time

amend_principle.text: serve short jobs ahead of long ones when the queue is deep
amend_principle.because: shortest-first clears a deep queue faster for everybody, including the long jobs

irreversible.text: decommission the old runner fleet and return the hardware

silence.about: how long a build is allowed to take
silence.rationale: a number would be set by whoever had the slowest build that quarter, and every team already argues its own case better than a limit would
silence.proposal: set a maximum build time for every pipeline

panel.rationale: three people to look at the preemption rule for a month
